Chapter 13 - Integration.correct_answer: $$y=x(x-1)(x+2)=x^3+x^2-2x$$ $$\int_{a}^{0}y\,dx=-\int_{0}^{1}y\,dx$$ $$-\left[\tfrac14 x^4+\tfrac13 x^3-x^2\right]_{a}^{0}=-\left[\tfrac14 x^4+\tfrac13 x^3-x^2\right]_{0}^{1}$$ $$-\left(0-\tfrac14 a^4-\tfrac13 a^3+a^2\right)=-\left(\tfrac14+\tfrac13-1\right)$$ $$-\tfrac14 a^4-\tfrac13 a^3+a^2=\tfrac{5}{12}\Rightarrow3a^4+4a^3-12a^2+5=0$$ $$\Rightarrow (a-1)^2(3a^2+10a+5)=0.$$

Chapter 13 - Integration.correct_answer: $$x^2+1=7-x\Rightarrow x^2+x-6=0\Rightarrow(x+3)(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x=-3,2$$ On $$[-3,0]$$ the line is above the curve, so $$A_{R_1}=\int_{-3}^{0}\big[(7-x)-(x^2+1)\big]\,dx=\int_{-3}^{0}(6-x-x^2)\,dx$$ $$=\left[6x-\tfrac12 x^2-\tfrac13 x^3\right]_{-3}^{0}=0-\left(-18-\tfrac92+9\right)=\tfrac{27}{2}$$ $$\text{Area of }R_1=\tfrac{27}{2}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 13 - Integration.question_text: The curve has equation $$y=\dfrac{2}{x^2}+x$$. Points $$A$$ and $$B$$ on the curve have $$x$$-coordinates $$\tfrac12$$ and $$2$$ respectively. Find the area of the finite region between chord $$AB$$ and the curve.

Chapter 13 - Integration.correct_answer: For $$x=\tfrac12$$, $$y_A=\dfrac{2}{(1/2)^2}+\tfrac12=8+\tfrac12=\tfrac{17}{2}$$; for $$x=2$$, $$y_B=\dfrac{2}{4}+2=\tfrac12+2=\tfrac52$$. Slope $$m=\dfrac{5/2-17/2}{2-1/2}=-4$$ so line $$AB$$ is $$y-5/2=-4(x-2)\Rightarrow y=-4x+\tfrac{21}{2}$$. Then $$A=\int_{1/2}^{2}\big((-4x+\tfrac{21}{2})-(\dfrac{2}{x^2}+x)\big)\,dx=\int_{1/2}^{2}\left(-5x+\tfrac{21}{2}-\dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)dx$$ $$=\left[-\tfrac{5}{2}x^2+\tfrac{21}{2}x+2x^{-1}\right]_{1/2}^{2}=\tfrac{27}{8}$$ $$\text{Area between }AB\text{ and the curve}=\tfrac{27}{8}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 13 - Integration.correct_answer: For the curve: $$y=3\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{4^3}+4=3\cdot2-\sqrt{64}+4=6-8+4=2$$. For the line: $$y=4-\tfrac12\cdot4=4-2=2$$. Thus both give $$y=2$$, so $$A(4,2)$$ is a point of intersection.

Chapter 13 - Integration.correct_answer: Setting $$3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4=4-\tfrac12 x$$ gives $$3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+\tfrac12 x=0$$. With substitution $$t=\sqrt{x}$$ this becomes $$t(3-t^2+\tfrac12 t^2)=t(3-\tfrac12 t^2)=0$$ so $$t=0$$ or $$t=\sqrt{6}$$; hence $$x=0,6$$, but only the portion shown is from $$x=0$$ to $$x=4$$ where the region is finite, bounded by the two curves. The area is $$A=\int_{0}^{4}\big(3\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x^3}+4-(4-\tfrac12 x)\big)\,dx=\int_{0}^{4}\left(3x^{1/2}-x^{3/2}+\tfrac12 x\right)dx$$ $$=\left[2x^{3/2}-\tfrac{2}{5}x^{5/2}+\tfrac14 x^2\right]_{0}^{4}=2\cdot8-\tfrac{2}{5}\cdot32+\tfrac14\cdot16=\tfrac{36}{5}$$ $$\text{Area of the finite region}=\tfrac{36}{5}\ \text{square units}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: (a) Using the substitution $$u=2^{x}$$, show that the equation $$4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0$$ can be written in the form $$u^{2}-2u-15=0$$. (b) Hence solve $$4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0$$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: Use $$4^{x}=(2^{2})^{x}=2^{2x}$$ and $$2^{x+1}=2\cdot2^{x}$$; then solve the quadratic in $$u$$ and back-substitute $$u=2^{x}$$.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$(a)\ 4^{x}-2^{x+1}-15=0\Rightarrow(2^{2})^{x}-2\cdot2^{x}-15=0\Rightarrow2^{2x}-2\cdot2^{x}-15=0.$$ With $$u=2^{x}$$ this becomes $$u^{2}-2u-15=0.$$ $$(b)\ u^{2}-2u-15=0\Rightarrow(u-5)(u+3)=0\Rightarrow u=5\ (\text{since }u>0).$$ Thus $$2^{x}=5\Rightarrow x=\log_{2}5=\dfrac{\ln5}{\ln2}\approx2.32\ \text{(2 d.p.)}.$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve the following equations, giving exact solutions: (a) $$\ln(2x-5)=8$$ (b) $$e^{4x}=5$$ (c) $$24-e^{-2x}=10$$ (d) $$\ln x+\ln(x-3)=0$$ (e) $$e^{x}+e^{-x}=2$$ (f) $$\ln2+\ln x=4$$.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: Rewrite logs/exponentials, isolate $$x$$ using $$e^{\ln y}=y$$ and standard algebra; for (e) set $$u=e^{x}$$.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$(a)\ \ln(2x-5)=8\Rightarrow2x-5=e^{8}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{e^{8}+5}{2}.$$ $$(b)\ e^{4x}=5\Rightarrow4x=\ln5\Rightarrow x=\tfrac14\ln5.$$ $$(c)\ 24-e^{-2x}=10\Rightarrow e^{-2x}=14\Rightarrow-2x=\ln14\Rightarrow x=-\tfrac12\ln14.$$ $$(d)\ \ln x+\ln(x-3)=\ln[x(x-3)]=0\Rightarrow x(x-3)=1\Rightarrow x^{2}-3x-1=0,$$ $$x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{13}}{2},\ \text{but domain }x>3\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3+\sqrt{13}}{2}.$$ $$(e)\ e^{x}+e^{-x}=2;\ \text{let }u=e^{x}\Rightarrow u+\dfrac1u=2\Rightarrow u^{2}-2u+1=0\Rightarrow(u-1)^{2}=0\Rightarrow u=1,$$ $$e^{x}=1\Rightarrow x=0.$$ $$(f)\ \ln2+\ln x=\ln(2x)=4\Rightarrow2x=e^{4}\Rightarrow x=\tfrac12e^{4}.$$
